notes: Asserted 2026-10-26 in app/production via api_request: the unauthenticated GET /health returned 200 with status ready, database ready, a boolean decisionsEnabled and Cache-Control no-store, the first passing assertion set recorded for the deployed health endpoint; shared capture failed with CONTEXT_INVALID so only this note and the private run evidence retain it.

Observed 2026-10-12 in reporting-test against the context-service host: using the existing caller-context token for reporting start returned 401 unauthorized, so caller-context access does not establish reporting/Decisions token compatibility.

Observed 2026-10-12 in reporting-test: the separate user-supplied REPORTING_API_TOKEN returned 200 for reporting start, load_crew_profile with the approved Avery phrase returned 200 with crm_context, and end returned 200, correcting the prior shared-token 401; Decisions and expert execution were not invoked.

On 2026-10-12 the repository-bound MCP client matched the setup binding but refused the authorized app/production POST with PRODUCTION_WRITE_REFUSED before any network attempt despite both saved launch registrations declaring API_ALLOW_PRODUCTION_WRITES=1, so binding identity alone did not establish that launch-policy changes had reached the running process; this is a client observation, not an API response.

Observed 2026-10-12 in reporting-test against the hailing-frequencies-app production URL using the reporting service CONTEXT_API_TOKEN: an empty JSON start body returned HTTP 401 unauthorized, so the configured service credential was rejected before session creation; the provider-side token value and deployment were not inspected.

Observed 2026-10-12 in reporting-test against the hailing-frequencies-app production URL: updating the reporting service to the replacement token supplied by the user changed the empty JSON start response from 401 unauthorized to 201 with authorization_required and a session token; the test session was explicitly ended afterward.

Observed 2026-10-12 against the deployed hailing-frequencies-app URL in reporting-test: authorize with session_token,name,authorization_phrase returned 400 invalid_body while start returned 201 and end returned 200, so rejection of the authorization body must not be described as service unavailability; deployed accepted field names were not established by this test.

Observed 2026-10-12 in reporting-test against the deployed hailing-frequencies-app URL: sending session_token,name,authorization returned 200 for the approved Avery Chen fixture, correcting the prior authorization_phrase request that returned 400 invalid_body; the diagnostic context session was ended successfully.

Observed 2026-10-12 in reporting-test: Avery Chen with authorization Alpha seven Bravo nine Echo two returned 200 with preferred_language english but no crew_member_id in the response or profile, so PR12 trusted Decisions intake still requires the identity API UUID addition rather than inferring an ID from name.

In the 2026-10-12 Avery browser rehearsal, crm_context reflected the pre-routing queue snapshot after a new task; refresh CRM context to display the newly queued task, based on local page behavior and service source rather than a Sannr client receipt.

Source inspection and injected-client tests on 2026-10-12 show that reason decisions_unavailable with null answers is returned before model classification when the Decisions client is disabled, so this shape cannot support threshold calibration or a gather-context instruction; this is local evidence, not a new production check.

Local source and fake regression on 2026-10-12 reproduce both supplied personal-log score sets: a valid expert route above 0.50 takes priority over missing details and an uncertain CRM issue match, using a general case with null equipment instead of inventing a match; access approval still requires a recorded expert result.

Local source inspection plus memory and disposable Postgres tests on 2026-10-12 show that a reporter crew row assigned to the intentionally nonexistent USS Nebraska is rejected as crew_member_not_found with reason ship_not_found before reporter-context storage, model classification or queue work; production behavior remains unverified until deployment.

Asserted 2026-10-26 in app/production via api_request: GET /events with an unknown scenario query returned 400 with Cache-Control no-store and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff before any event stream opened, so the fixture name is validated up front and the error path can be checked without holding an SSE connection.
